PullRequest.Title: update json/html services
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activating the built-in HTML or JSON language extension and starting its language server
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Extension activation constructs one language client, launches one node IPC server or one browser worker, performs the LSP initialize exchange, and awaits client.start() before feature registration completes. The dependency versions change, but the diff does not add another launch, initialization request, or synchronous startup operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the node language-server module (or create one web worker in browser builds).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One launch per extension activation, plus one replacement after a coalesced participant-change restart.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same LanguageClient construction, process/worker launch, and awaited start occurred before the package-version updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial launch and LSP handshake are on the feature-availability critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: LSP initialize/start handshake between extension host and language server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialization exchange per launched server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous client/server versions used the same handshake at the same call sites and cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before language features become ready.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read extension package metadata and create the JSON schema-cache directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One package read per activation; one recursive mkdir per JSON activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical package-read and cache-directory setup occurred before the dependency updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations occur before client.start(); HTML's package read is synchronous, but both operations predate the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One client/server pair per activated built-in language extension; participant changes can trigger a restart, but existing code coalesces those changes with a single 2-second timer.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: HTML and JSON each run one server independently. Within each extension, participant-triggered restarts are serialized by disposing the old client before starting the replacement, and repeated triggers are coalesced by replacing the pending timer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No startup result cache is involved. JSON initializes its existing persistent schema cache once; HTML discovers custom-data URIs once. Neither cache lifecycle is changed by these dependency-only hunks.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that launch, handshake, restart coalescing, and visible boundary cardinality are unchanged; low confidence in any unobservable internal package implementation delta, so no regression mechanism is established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The internal startup cost differences between the old prerelease packages and new published packages are not available in the repository diff, so exact bytecode, allocation, and timing deltas cannot be measured from repository evidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff swaps compatible dependency versions and lockfile resolutions without adding startup work, changing launch count, or moving an existing boundary onto a hotter path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Editing HTML/JSON documents: synchronization, validation, completion, hover, symbols, formatting, and related language requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each editor operation is serialized over the existing LSP client/server transport and then invokes the corresponding language-service method. JSON reuses a bounded parsed-document cache; HTML caches per-document settings and mode models. The changed manifests do not alter handlers, request frequency, result limits, cancellation flow, or document synchronization mode.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send incremental text synchronization and feature requests/results between the extension host and language-server process/worker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transport exchange per existing synchronization or feature request; result payload scales with the existing bounded/unbounded feature result semantics.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old LSP client, protocol, JSON-RPC, and server packages occupied the same transport path with the same handlers and request cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Feature responses are on the interactive completion/hover/diagnostic critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Encode/decode LSP requests and responses, including diagnostics, completion items, symbols, and edits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per existing protocol message; payload size follows document edits and feature results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous dependency versions already serialized the same messages at the same boundaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization is part of each IPC request/response path, but no changed implementation or increased payload/cardinality is present in the supplied diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with document size, open-document count, edit frequency, and requested result count. Effective request cardinality remains one protocol operation per editor feature invocation or document synchronization event, not one new boundary per syntax node or result item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The language server handles requests through the existing JSON-RPC connection with cancellation tokens passed to feature handlers. Validation scheduling and request concurrency are unchanged by the manifest-only diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: JSON's parsed-document model cache remains bounded to 10 entries with a 60-second cleanup interval. HTML's scoped settings are cached by document URI and removed on close; both servers dispose model resources on shutdown. No key, bound, invalidation, or allocation policy changes in the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that repository-visible hot-path cardinality, cache bounds, cancellation, and result limits are unchanged. There is insufficient evidence for a concrete regression inside the upgraded packages.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Published dependency internals are not included in the patch, so small implementation-level CPU or allocation changes cannot be ruled out; there is no code, benchmark, or transitive dependency evidence of increased work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Version replacement alone does not prove changed expensive work, frequency, scale, or lifetime, and the lockfiles add no new runtime dependency or fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Loading HTML custom-data files and JSON schemas during initialization, configuration changes, and validation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: HTML sends custom-data URIs to the server and reads each requested URI through an existing client filesystem/document request. JSON validation resolves referenced schemas through existing file/client requests; remote schemas may require network access before validation completes. These paths and their placement are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read HTML custom-data content from workspace/extension storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per language-service load of each deduplicated configured URI; edits/configuration changes can invalidate and reload through the existing path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same custom-data inventory, IPC request, and filesystem/document read path existed before the version changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Custom-data availability waits for the relevant content request, but server startup does not await the initial fetch promise.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request custom-data or non-file JSON schema content from the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per distinct content resolution initiated by the existing language service; no diff-visible increase in distinct URIs or retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same custom request types and handlers were used with the prior protocol packages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The requested content must arrive before that data/schema can be consumed; it is off the initial HTML initialize response path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download remote JSON schema content with redirects and optional ETag revalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold or expired cache: one HTTP request per distinct requested schema URI; warm schemastore cache under 48 hours: zero network calls; ETag cache: one conditional request, with one fallback request only if cached content is unexpectedly unavailable after 304.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical request-light version, request service, ETag policy, and call sites existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold schema validation waits for the network response; warm cached reads avoid the network.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write/delete persistent JSON schema cache files and update cache metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file write after a cacheable successful download; one file read per warm-cache hit or 304 reuse; clear-cache is explicitly user-triggered and scales with cached files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The cache implementation and lifecycle are unchanged by the dependency updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Warm reads and cache writes are awaited on schema resolution; clear-cache is command-driven.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: HTML work scales with the deduplicated Set of configured custom-data URIs. JSON work scales with distinct referenced schema URIs after language-service caching; schemastore HTTP content is additionally served from a persistent cache for up to 48 hours before revalidation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: HTML custom-data loads are initiated by the existing language-service fetch flow. JSON schema requests are request-driven over the single LSP connection; no new Promise.all fan-out, limiter removal, or concurrency burst appears in the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: JSON schemastore entries use persistent ETag/file caching and a 48-hour warm-cache window; 304 responses read cached files and avoid downloading content. HTML deduplicates URI inventories with Sets but reads content when requested. The dependency updates do not change these repository-owned cache keys, invalidation, negative-cache behavior, or cleanup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the existing boundary locations, cache behavior, and repository-owned cardinality; insufficient confidence that the upgraded language-service packages increase request count or defeat caching.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A new language-service implementation could theoretically alter when it asks for custom data or schemas, but the patch contains no dependency source, tests, call-count change, or evidence showing increased requests. Existing lockfile changes only show version substitutions and some type-package deduplication.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. All filesystem, IPC, and network boundaries predate the diff, and there is no evidence that the upgrades increase their cardinality, concurrency, or critical-path placement.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed manifests/lockfiles and traced activation, interactive LSP traffic, custom-data loading, and schema loading. The updates replace existing telemetry, URI, language-client/server/protocol, and language-service versions without adding dependencies or changing repository-visible calls, caching, concurrency, lifecycle, or boundary cardinality. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue or provable regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
